tool.name: Geomasking

param.name: workspace
param.dialogReference: The File Geodatabase used to stage intermediate spatial processing layers and store the ingested features.

param.name: village_table
param.dialogReference: The input CSV file containing source village points. Must include coordinate columns (Latitude, Longitude), an identifier (FNID), and the administrative boundary linkage key (ADM1ADM2).

param.name: boundaries
param.datatype: Layer or Shapefile or Feature Class
param.dialogReference: The polygon feature layer, feature class, or shapefile defining the administrative containment boundaries within which displaced points must remain.

param.name: max_distance
param.dialogReference: The maximum geodesic distance in meters that a point can be shifted from its original position.

param.name: min_distance
param.dialogReference: The minimum geodesic distance in meters that a point must be shifted from its original position. Must be less than the maximum distance.

param.name: out_disp_name
param.dialogReference: The destination feature class that will contain the relocated points and updated coordinate fields.

param.name: out_dir
param.dialogReference: The folder directory where the summary table (Displacement_output.csv) will be written.

tool.summary:
The Geomasking tool applies spatial displacement to sensitive point coordinates (such as village, community, or survey cluster locations) to protect participant privacy while preserving spatial validity for aggregated analytical workflows.

For each point, the tool calculates a geodesic annular buffer zone constrained between user-defined minimum and maximum displacement distances. It clips the candidate buffer to a specified administrative restriction polygon (e.g., district, department, or admin boundary) and randomly generates candidate locations within the allowable area. The point is then relocated to a randomly selected candidate position within its respective administrative boundary, and the resulting dataset is exported as both an updated geodatabase feature class and a companion CSV table.
tool.usage:
• Input Data Format: The tool accepts point tables in CSV format containing FNID, Latitude, Longitude, and the concatenation key field specified for administrative boundary restriction (default: ADM1ADM2).

  • Boundary Restrictions: Polygons supplied in the boundary parameter determine the containment zone. Points will never be displaced outside of the administrative boundary polygon with matching identification attributes.

  • Geodesic Accuracy: Buffering operations use geodesic calculations. This prevents spatial distortion and scale variation when evaluating displacement distances (in meters) over geographic coordinate systems (such as WGS 1984 / EPSG 4326).

  • Attribute Retention: Baseline coordinates are preserved in the output feature class under old_Latitude and old_Longitude alongside the new, displaced Latitude and Longitude values.

  • Fallback Behavior: If a point's displacement buffer falls entirely outside the boundary polygon (for example, on an extreme coastal edge, border vertex, or narrow spit), the tool falls back to restricting candidate sampling directly to the administrative boundary polygon to ensure processing completes without missing records.

scriptExample.title: Python Syntax Example
scriptExample.code:
import arcpy
# Import the Python Toolbox (.pyt) arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\Geomasking\Script\geomasking.pyt")
# Execute Geomasking arcpy.toolbox.Geomasking( workspace=r"C:\Geomasking\geomasked.gdb", village_table=r"C:\Geomasking\Test data\Ihorombe_villages.csv", boundaries=r"C:\Geomasking\boundaries\MG_ADMIN_2018\MG_Admin2_2018.shp", max_distance=3000, min_distance=1000, out_disp_name=r"C:\Geomasking\geomasked.gdb\Displaced_Ihorombe_villages", out_dir=r"C:\Geomasking\Output" )
